principle_text: When the seller highlights the positive attributes of the item without addressing price adjustments, avoid focusing solely on gathering information or building rapport to prevent weakening negotiation leverage.
When the seller confirms good condition and recent ownership of the item, avoid providing information that could strengthen the buyer's leverage without progressing towards a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item's excellent condition, avoid failing to leverage this information to negotiate a lower price or propose a counteroffer.
When the seller establishes a firm asking price above the buyer's initial offer, avoid asking for the price without first anchoring a lower offer to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller highlights the item's good condition despite minor flaws, avoid prematurely using this information to push for a lower price without proposing a counteroffer or negotiating leverage.
When the seller emphasizes the excellent condition and heritage of the item, avoid asking questions about scratches or age that do not directly challenge the price or leverage your initial offer.
When the seller sets a high initial price and requests a security deposit, avoid revealing financial limitations or desperation as it may weaken your negotiation leverage.

When the seller states the phone is brand new and still in the package, avoid engaging in casual small talk or anecdotes unrelated to price negotiation to ensure focus on the negotiation goal.

When the buyer makes a slightly reduced offer from their initial price, like $725 instead of $735, the seller may be more inclined to offer a lower price, such as $700, leading to a stronger negotiation position for the buyer.

When the seller restates the initial price without engaging in price discussion, avoid making requests that do not directly address the price difference to prevent stagnation in negotiation progress.

When the seller emphasizes the collectible and classic value of an item, avoid asking purely factual questions that allow the seller to reinforce their price justification.
